title: Showing an Action in Progress
goal: Use Norwegian activity frames to highlight actions happening right now or around a past moment.

objectives.statement: Use Norwegian activity frames to highlight actions happening right now or around a past moment.

spans.value: Jonas is meeting friends at a community hall for their weekly quiz night. He is late, so Ida calls him.
Hvor er du? Vi venter på deg.

blocks.translation: Where are you? We’re waiting for you.

spans.value: Jeg er rett utenfor. Jeg holder på å låse sykkelen.

blocks.translation: I’m just outside. I’m locking my bike.

spans.value: Bra. Sara sitter og gjør spørsmålene klare, og Amir står og lager kaffe.

blocks.translation: Good. Sara is sitting and getting the questions ready, and Amir is standing and making coffee.

spans.value: Jeg kommer inn om et minutt.

blocks.translation: I’ll be inside in a minute.

spans.value: Jeg ringte deg tidligere også. Hva gjorde du da?

blocks.translation: I called you earlier too. What were you doing then?

spans.value: Da du ringte, sto jeg og ventet på bussen.

blocks.translation: When you called, I was standing and waiting for the bus.

spans.value: Så du meldingen min?
Ja. På bussen satt jeg og leste meldingene, men jeg glemte å svare.

blocks.translation: Yes. On the bus I was sitting and reading the messages, but I forgot to reply.

spans.value: The friends use ordinary present and past tense, but several sentences place an action under a spotlight. They show what someone is in the middle of doing now or what was happening around a particular past moment.

Norwegian can express this progressive meaning (progressiv betydning) through several activity frames. Unlike English, Norwegian does not need a direct equivalent of be + verb-ing in every such sentence.
Compare these two sentences:

no.value: Jeg låser sykkelen.

en.value: I lock the bike. / I’m locking the bike.

no.value: Jeg holder på å låse sykkelen.

en.value: I’m in the middle of locking the bike.

spans.value: The simple present can already describe something happening now, especially when the context makes the time clear. The activity frame holder på å gives the action extra focus. Jonas is not reporting a general habit. He is explaining what is occupying him at that exact moment.
The same contrast is possible in the past:

no.value: Jeg lagde kaffe.

en.value: I made coffee. / I was making coffee.

no.value: Jeg holdt på å lage kaffe.

en.value: I was in the middle of making coffee.

spans.value: The simple past reports the action. The frame holdt på å highlights the action as ongoing around a past moment.
The most general frame in this lesson is:
holde på å + infinitive
The first verb carries the tense. The activity after å remains in the infinitive.
Present time

no.value: Jeg holder på å låse sykkelen.
Vi holder på å gjøre klart rommet.
Sara holder på å skrive spørsmålene.
Amir holder på å lage kaffe.

spans.value: The present form is holder:

no.value: Nå holder jeg på å rydde bordet.
Hva holder dere på å gjøre?

spans.value: Past time
For an action in progress around a past moment, use the past form holdt:

no.value: Klokka sju holdt jeg på å spise middag.

en.value: At seven o’clock I was eating dinner.

no.value: Vi holdt på å gjøre klart rommet da lyset gikk.

en.value: We were getting the room ready when the lights went out.

no.value: Sara holdt på å skrive et spørsmål da Ida kom.

en.value: Sara was writing a question when Ida arrived.

no.value: Hva holdt du på å gjøre da jeg ringte?

en.value: What were you doing when I called?

spans.value: Notice that only the first verb changes:
Time: now

no.value: holder på å lage

spans.value: Time: past moment

no.value: holdt på å lage

spans.value: The infinitive lage does not become lagde after å.
Compact rule

statement.value: to highlight an activity happening now. Use
to highlight an activity happening around a past moment.

spans.value: A common mistake
Do not copy the English structure by placing er before a present-tense verb.
Incorrect:

no.value: Jeg er lager kaffe.

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Jeg lager kaffe.

spans.value: More explicitly ongoing:

no.value: Jeg holder på å lage kaffe.

en.value: I’m in the middle of making coffee.

spans.value: Norwegian simple present often covers both English simple-present and present-progressive meanings. The activity frame is available when the ongoing nature of the action matters.

sections.title: Showing posture as well as activity

spans.value: Norwegian can also describe an ongoing scene with a posture verb:
These frames say both what position someone is in and what that person is doing.

no.value: Sara sitter og skriver.
Amir står og lager kaffe.

en.value: Amir is standing and making coffee.

no.value: Katten ligger og sover under bordet.

en.value: The cat is lying and sleeping under the table.

spans.value: In natural English, the posture may be translated explicitly or left in the background:

no.value: Sara sitter og gjør spørsmålene klare.

en.value: Sara is sitting and getting the questions ready. / Sara is getting the questions ready.

spans.value: The Norwegian sentence creates a small visual scene. Sara is seated, and getting the questions ready is the activity in progress.
Use a posture frame only when the posture makes sense in the situation. If you do not know or care whether someone is sitting, standing, or lying down, holde på å is more neutral.
Compare:

no.value: Sara holder på å lese spørsmålene.
Sara sitter og leser spørsmålene.

en.value: Sara is sitting and reading the questions.

spans.value: Both highlight an ongoing activity. The second also tells us how Sara is positioned.

sections.title: Posture frames in present and past time

spans.value: In a posture frame, both verbs are ordinary tense forms joined by og.
Present

no.value: Jeg sitter og leser.
Hun står og venter.
De ligger og hviler.

spans.value: Past

no.value: Jeg satt og leste.
Hun sto og ventet.
De lå og hvilte.

en.value: They were lying down and resting.

spans.value: The pattern changes like this:
Now

no.value: sitter og leser
står og venter
ligger og sover

spans.value: Around a past moment

no.value: satt og leste
sto og ventet
lå og sov

spans.value: This differs from holde på å:

no.value: Jeg holdt på å lese.
Jeg satt og leste.

spans.value: Here, lese is an infinitive because it follows å.
Here, leste is past tense. Both satt and leste locate the scene in the past.
Common form errors
Incorrect:

no.value: I går satt jeg og leser.

en.value: 'Incorrect: Yesterday I was sitting and reading.'

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: I går satt jeg og leste.

en.value: Yesterday I was sitting and reading.

spans.value: Incorrect:

no.value: Da du ringte, sto jeg å ventet.

en.value: 'Incorrect: When you called, I was standing and waiting.'

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Da du ringte, sto jeg og ventet.

en.value: When you called, I was standing and waiting.

spans.value: Use å in holde på å, but og in the posture frames:

no.value: Jeg holder på å vente.
Jeg står og venter.

spans.value: Time expressions often make the choice clear.
Happening now

no.value: Akkurat nå holder vi på å finne et ledig bord.

en.value: Right now we’re looking for a free table.

no.value: Se, Ida står og snakker med vakten.

en.value: Look, Ida is standing and talking to the attendant.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke snakke lenge. Jeg holder på å gå inn.

en.value: I can’t talk for long. I’m going inside.

spans.value: Happening around a past moment

no.value: Klokka halv åtte satt vi og ventet på Jonas.

en.value: At half past seven we were sitting and waiting for Jonas.

no.value: Da Jonas kom inn, sto Amir og helte kaffe i koppene.

en.value: When Jonas came in, Amir was standing and pouring coffee into the cups.

no.value: Da telefonen ringte, holdt Sara på å lese det første spørsmålet.

en.value: When the phone rang, Sara was reading the first question.

spans.value: A past activity frame often supplies the background for a shorter event:

no.value: Jeg holdt på å låse sykkelen da Ida ringte.

en.value: I was locking my bike when Ida called.

spans.value: The lesson focus is the ongoing background activity: holdt på å låse. The call identifies the moment around which that activity was in progress.
Jonas enters the hall and sees the scene Ida described.
Nå er jeg her. Hva holder dere på å gjøre?

blocks.translation: Now I’m here. What are you doing?

spans.value: Vi holder på å dele oss i lag.
Hvor er Sara?
Hun sitter og snakker med den nye deltakeren. Amir står og teller kaffekoppene.

blocks.translation: She’s sitting and talking with the new participant. Amir is standing and counting the coffee cups.

spans.value: Jeg kan hjelpe med lagene nå. Da du ringte tidligere, sto jeg og ventet på bussen, men nå er jeg klar.

blocks.translation: I can help with the teams now. When you called earlier, I was standing and waiting for the bus, but now I’m ready.

spans.value: Fint. Hjelp med lagene mens jeg hjelper Amir.

blocks.translation: Good. Help with the teams while I help Amir.

spans.value: The scene has moved forward, but the same forms remain useful. Jonas asks about activity in progress now. He also returns to the earlier phone call and describes what he was doing at that past moment.

One detail deserves care: holdt på å works most clearly here with activities that can continue for some time, such as cooking, reading, preparing, or locking something. With certain sudden events, it can instead suggest that something nearly happened:

no.value: Jeg holdt på å falle.

spans.value: For this chapter’s target meaning, use holde på å with clearly ongoing activities.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: preparing for a birthday visit

spans.value: Imagine a different everyday situation. You arrive at a friend’s flat while several people are preparing a birthday meal. One person calls to ask what everyone is doing. Later, you explain what was happening when the birthday guest arrived unexpectedly.

Without looking back, explain the difference between holder på å lage and står og lager. Then change both frames to describe a past moment. Finish by writing one sentence with a taught present-time activity frame about something happening around you now and one sentence with a taught past-time activity frame about what you were doing at a specific time yesterday.

prompt.value: Read the comparison in the stem and choose the interpretation that matches the contrast between neutral tense reporting and explicit ongoing focus.

options.text: «Jeg lagde kaffe.» — I was in the middle of making coffee. «Jeg holdt på å lage kaffe.» — I made coffee: a neutral report.
options.why: This reverses the meanings of the simple past and the activity frame.

options.text: «Jeg lagde kaffe.» and «Jeg holdt på å lage kaffe.» both report the action neutrally; the frame adds no extra ongoing focus.
options.why: The frame explicitly highlights the activity as ongoing.

options.text: «Jeg lagde kaffe.» — I made coffee: a neutral report. «Jeg holdt på å lage kaffe.» — I was in the middle of making coffee: explicit ongoing focus.
options.why: The simple past reports the action, while holdt på å highlights the activity as ongoing around the past moment.

options.why: The first sentence gives the wrong posture for the person at the bus stop.

options.why: The second sentence unnecessarily claims that Amir is standing.

options.text: 1. Hun står og venter på bussen. — She is standing and waiting for the bus. 2. Amir holder på å lage kaffe. — Amir is making coffee.
options.why: The first frame shows visible standing posture; the second highlights the activity without claiming a posture.

prompt.value: Write a short Norwegian description of a new birthday-visit scene. Describe several people preparing a meal now: someone is decorating the room, someone is cooking, someone is waiting by the door, and someone is resting briefly on a sofa. Use holder på å + infinitive when posture is irrelevant, and use a present posture frame such as sitter og, står og, or ligger og when posture is meaningful. Use birthday-visit wording.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants when they preserve the requested meanings and frame forms; do not require exact wording.

criteria.instruction: Describes decorating, cooking, waiting by the door, and resting on a sofa in natural Norwegian.
Uses present-time activity frames to show actions happening now.
Uses at least one present holder på å + infinitive frame when posture is irrelevant.
Uses at least one present posture frame with sitter og, står og, or ligger og when posture is meaningful.
Uses wording appropriate to the birthday-visit situation.

Use birthday-visit wording.
